title: The Hermit Monk
text: A monk who has not spoken in forty years sits by the road to the shrines, thin as a stick, his beard to his knees. His eyes are kind. He holds up a slate with chalk letters on it, written long ago and never wiped: ASK ME ONE THING.

options.label: Ask him the way. It is the safest thing to ask.

outcomes.text: For the first time in forty years he wipes the slate, then draws a map. His hand shakes with the effort.

options.label: The wisest asks about the House's future, though the answer may not be kind.

outcomes.text: He writes one word and weeps, refusing to wipe it away. They cannot stop thinking about it.

options.label: Ask for his blessing, and carry it with you on the road.

outcomes.text: He touches each brow with a chalky thumb. The dust stays all day.
